answer.evidence: The machine is a pink header (rows 1-10), a dark glass window (rows 11-21) and a wider base (rows 22-31). The base's control deck is a lighter pink band at rows 22-26, with button marks, a darker edge line at row 26 and shadow at rows 27-28. The front panel with coin slot sits below it (rows 27-31), so the deck reads as a top surface. The header is 7 flat pink rows with a darker line at row 8, a highlight at row 9 and shadow at row 10. That is ambiguous, since it could be a front-facing marquee, but it counts weakly as a top band. The window and base give 14+ rows of front face. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 21 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it is at or above the comparable references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, which means the outline leans toward a dark maroon/pink of the cabinet instead of a black sticker line. The pink body shows a highlight, light, mid and dark ramp. The glass window with prizes and the control panel add varied shapes and small clusters. It is a little less textured than the stall or well, but a careful artist would accept it beside them without it looking thinner or flatter.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts: the candidate has 21 visible tones per 16x16 tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. That is on par with the stall (17) and the well (20), and above the hedge (9). The outline is tinted, a dark magenta/red-brown beside the pink body, not black. By eye the candidate is small and clean, and the pink cabinet reads with about 3-4 steps (light pink, mid, dark, deep) plus a glass window with a few toys. Beodeul props like the well and stall show 5-6 steps, per-tile highlights and grain. The candidate's cabinet face is smoother, with little speckle or grain, and the prize interior is only a few pixels of detail. It is not a flat sticker, since the tinted outline, the glass highlights and the toy clusters give real variation, but it is somewhat below the richest references. Slightly lower than the references on shading depth and surface texture, so I fail it under the 'when in doubt' rule.

answer.evidence: The main cabinet (rows 1-21) is a face-on elevation. The header (rows 1-10) is uniform pink with a darker row 8, a light sign strip at row 9 and a dark row 10. It is the same width as the glass body, so it reads as a vertical marquee panel with no top surface, only a 1-row rim at row 1. The glass window (rows 11-21) shows the claw and prizes face-on. Only the wider base (width 26 from row 22) has a lighter ledge, rows 22-26, with a button and joystick. That is a small control-panel top below a large flat elevation, not a top on the main body. The tall header is drawn as a vertical face only, where a horizontal top would be expected.

styleAnswer.evidence: The claw machine reads as a prop of the same kind and scale as the stall and well. Its measured density is 21 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The pink cabinet shows highlight, mid and dark steps, and the glass window holds several small toys in different tones, which gives it clustered detail. The cabinet has about 5 steps, slightly fewer than the references' 5-6, but the density and outline facts are at reference level, so a careful artist would accept it beside the stall and well.
